newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to combat U.S. "Free Asia" broadcasts.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to combat U.S. "Free Asia" broadcasts.

text.p: Hanoi said on Friday it would step up internal vigilance and increase domestic propaganda in response to plans by U.S. radio station Radio Free Asia to begin broadcasts to Vietnam next week.

A commentary in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper described the U.S.-funded station as "an assault tool of the hostile forces", and said its plans to begin broadcasts in Vietnamese were aimed at political sabotage.

"It's too clear that like Radio 'Free Europe', RFA is a product of the Cold War period, a tool of cultural and ideological aggression to interfere in the internal affairs of Asian countries," Nhan Dan said, adding:

"We are determined to heighten vigilance and carry out effective countermeasures, including ideological work and cultural and press activities to expose the distortions aimed at sabotaging Vietnam's revolution..."
Radio Free Asia said this week it would begin broadcasts to Burma on February 4 and to Vietnam on February 6 -- the eve of the Lunar New Year and start of the traditional Tet holiday.

Programmes, containing a mixture of news, commentary and entertainment, will start at 30 minutes and expand eventually to one hour. A statement said RFA would follow strict standards of fairness and objectivity.
The station, which was created by Congress, has been broadcasting in Mandarin Chinese and Tibetan for several months, and plans to extend its service to Cambodia, Laos and North Korea this year.
China and Vietnam are among several countries that have condemned the station.
Nhan Dan said the experience of RFA's first few months showed its programmes "always contain obvious incitements and hostility towards China's government..."
